subject: stack
text: - Process liveness: sysinfo's process start time is also the observed side of the server check each frame-writing client makes before its first frame (the connected peer's pid and its start time against the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at`; §Standard Contracts, Session liveness).

subject: dec-message-broker-ipc
text: - A verified client meets an unreadable or newer snapshot as an absent one, through `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` (§Standard Contracts, Snapshot envelope): a replayed snapshot holds no `endpoint`, so it gives no endpoint and no frame is written; no product reader under `src/` calls `read_snapshot`.

subject: dec-mcp
text:
- **[MCP] rmcp 3.4.1, stdio, tools `send · wait · last · answer · list`. `release` is CLI-only.** Refusals are `isError: true` tool results mapped from `result.refusal`. Rationale: it is the official SDK, tracks spec 2026-07-28, and the pinned minor limits churn from its near-weekly releases. `answer` and `list` are how a driver answers dialogs under R7 and sees sessions, and the prototype driver uses both every session. `release` stays off the driver's tool surface, so a driver is never offered a way to hand the wheel back to automation. This is an affordance, not an enforcement: an agent's Bash tool can still run CLI `viola release` (for example through `VIOLA_BIN`), and the Local endpoint trust boundary accepts it because v1 trusts every process of the same OS user. The wrapper refuses a `release` whose `params` carry a string `from` (`-32602`, `data.reason` `release-from-driver`), so CLI `viola release` run inside a wrapped session (`VIOLA_NAME` set) is refused; `from` is self-reported (`from_trust:"self-reported"`), so this deters rather than enforces. `pause`, `link` and `unlink` are CLI-only for the same reason: they are human controls over the wheel and the link topology, and links made by drivers are already recorded from `from` on `send` and `answer`. Tool inputs:
  - `send {target, text}`
  - `wait {target, after?, timeout_ms?}`
  - `last {target}`
  - `answer {target, dialog_id, response}`, with `response` in the channel `answer` shape
  - `list {}`

  `target` is a `ViolaName`, and the server adds `from` from its own `VIOLA_NAME` only when it has a name of its own. As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): each handler takes the raw argument object and re-validates it, a schema violation being the `invalid-params` result with a closed field `detail` and no frame (§Conventions, Error handling schema), and an internal handler fault being the JSON-RPC error `-32603` `internal error` with `data: null`; MCP `wait` sends `timeout_ms` = `min(given, 50 000)` (`viola_mcp::WAIT_CAP`, `wait_timeout`), 50 000 ms when none is given, and `after` as given. The bound sits below claude 2.1.287's stdio tool-call default, which exceeds 50 s (as measured live at that chunk, `evidence/live-mcp.md` start 2: a default `wait` answered `timed-out` at 50 012 ms with no client timeout; the exact default is unmeasured). `list` builds the CLI's board and makes its one `claude agents --json` read (§Standard Contracts, Session liveness; the founder's own answer, that chunk's `inputs#I2` Q1).

subject: dec-mcp
text: - Each frame tool (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`) runs `viola_state::strict::check_instance` on the home and the target's instance directory before `live_endpoint`; a refusal is the `instance-unreachable` result with `detail: null`, no frame and no line.

subject: dec-links
text: - The explicit verbs run `viola_state::strict::check_instance` on the home and `instances/<driven>` through `client::refuse_untrusted` (`src/cmd/client.rs`, shared with the six frame verbs) before `client::start`, so ahead of any role file, log or snapshot read, because opening a log narrows an existing home to 0700 and a check made after it passes a home at 0770; a refusal is exit 21. Then come the liveness-only pre-check (`live_endpoint`), the server identity check through `cmd::client::connect`, and one request.

subject: dec-cli-version-compatibility
text:
- **[CLI Version Compatibility] Per-behaviour capability ledger + transport-only degrade + `viola verify` re-stamp.** Ledger rows:
  - S3: AskUserQuestion via PreToolUse `updatedInput`.
  - S7: ExitPlanMode approves only through PreToolUse, as `allow` + `updatedInput` set to the tool's own input, unchanged (a non-object input gives `{}`); revise via `deny` + `message`. A bare `allow` left the plan dialog up on live 2.1.288 (the founder's live ruling after step 0's STOP 7, 2026-10-05).
  - S8: free text and `annotations`.
  - The R8 identity floor: the measured `CLAUDE*` parent-identity names stripped even when the persistent environment defines them (every other `CLAUDE*` name follows the prefix rule, see Occupied Resources → Environment variables).
  - npm-shim → `claude.exe` resolution.
  - Statusline `rate_limits.*`, the settings-override mechanism, and the shell Claude Code runs a statusline command through on each OS. Rows `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `statusline-rate-limits` since chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, relied only where the status line is wrapped (`statusline::WRAPPED_HERE`, Unix): on Unix the statusline pass-through and, since chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor, the budget gate's `budget-paused` refusal rest on stamped rows; the Windows legs are owed to "Windows-only live measurements" (§Cross-cutting Patterns, Capability ledger).
  - Harness prompt prefixes: `<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message`, `<cross-session-message` (compiled, matched on the raw start). As measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host, `evidence/scratch-session.md`): a real cross-session message reaches UserPromptSubmit unescaped, as `<cross-session-message from="…" from-name="…" from-mode="…">`, a newline, the text, a newline and `</cross-session-message>`, and the plain prefix files it `harness`; a `<task-notification>` typed at the very start of a prompt arrives as typed, so a human who types it first is filed `harness` (see Tag escaping). The escaped cross-session form rests on a relayed measurement alone (overseer1's F115 on andromeda-worker, the viola-lab prototype's `harness_injected`); it was not seen in that session and stays compiled. On the CLI the builder session itself runs (PATH `claude`, read by counts only, the same chunk's `evidence/harness-prompts-driver-log.md`) the `<agent-message from=` and `<task-notification>` forms reach the hook starting at the tag, with no preface. These readings came from a scratch probe, not a `viola verify` probe, so the harness-prefix ledger row stays owed.
  - The long-paste wrapper (row `long-paste-wrapper`): the CLI's own pair arrives unescaped, `<pasted_content id="X">\n…\n</pasted_content id="X">`, the close repeating the id (981 bytes wrapped, 749 not, on 2.1.280; the close form as measured at chunk 2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events research.md M5), and the CLI frames it: two newlines directly before the open tag and, after the close tag, one newline at the prompt's end, two when typed text follows, and three in all between two adjacent pairs. The lone-paste frame is as measured on 2.1.287 in four live sessions at chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows (`evidence/step0-shapes.md`, `rehearsal-shapes.md`, `record-round-green.md`: a 1 500-byte one-line paste wrapped, a 200-byte paste not); the frame beside typed text and between two pairs is as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host (`evidence/scratch-session.md`). The id is 4 hex characters: every pair of one session carried the same id, the two pairs of one prompt included, and it differed between sessions (as measured at the same two chunks). `viola-agent-claude` (`hook::unwrap_pastes`) unwraps only that exact same-id pair and removes that frame with it, nothing wider: the two newlines before the open tag, the one after the close, and a second after the close when text follows that is not the next pair's own two-newline frame. A third newline before, a second after at the prompt's end and a lone one before stay, an open tag with no matching close removes nothing, and everything else outside a pair is kept byte for byte.
 A pasted text's own last newline never reaches the hook (as measured at the 2026-10-07 chunk, `evidence/scratch-session.md`, `live-shape-red-green.md`): for a wrapped text that ends in a newline the CLI adds none before the close tag, so its prompt is byte for byte that of the same text without the newline, and an unwrapped text loses its last newline too; `text` is then the pasted text less that newline. The measurement stands and no `send` relies on it: `send` never types a text that ends in a newline ([Delivery Confirmation]). The frame beside typed text and between two pairs is compiled on that one measurement and held by `hook.rs` unit cases only: no `viola verify` run types those shapes (Run B pastes each compiled text alone), so the `long-paste-wrapper` row re-validates only the lone-paste frame per CLI version. No probe is owed for them: a shape no `send` relies on needs no probe (the founder's live ruling on the ledger rule, 2026-10-07T11:37Z, relayed by the overseer). They arise only when a human types beside a paste, so no claim and no wheel decision rests on them; after a CLI change a human's own prompt `text` may carry a stray newline until it is noticed. Read statically from the 2.1.287 binary, not measured: the wrap threshold (over 800 characters or more than 2 lines) and the feature flag behind the wrapping. Unmeasured: a long or a repeated text pasted while the paste hint stands.
  - Modal and input-box screen signatures.
  - The hook tier map.
  - Turn end without Stop: which hook, if any, fires when a turn ends on an API error (Stop does not fire on a user interrupt), so the running-turn state can be cleared.
  - Dialog concurrency: whether two dialog hooks (PreToolUse `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`, PermissionRequest) can be open at once in one session, for example on parallel tool calls.
  - `claude agents --json` join field (row `agents-join`): a row exposes both the child pid (`pid`) and the session id (`sessionId`) that match a wrapped instance, as measured on 2.1.287 (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board: the record round's `agents-join` pass, `stamped 2.1.287  23 pass  0 fail`, on the Linux dev host; its Windows reading owed on "Windows-only live measurements"). The row is relied on every OS and probed by Run B's one agents read (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 1 of that chunk, `inputs#I1`, relayed verbatim by the operator).
  - Local commands: built-in local commands fire no UserPromptSubmit (measured: `/remote-control`), so the ledger lists each known local command with its delivery post-condition or "none" (compiled, `ledger::LOCAL_COMMANDS`). For `/clear` it is a SessionStart with source `clear` and a new `session_id` (row `local-command-clear`): as measured on 2.1.287 in `viola verify`'s Run B (chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows, `evidence/rehearsal-shapes.md`), a pasted `/clear` fires SessionEnd (`reason` `clear`), then SessionStart (`source` `clear`, a new `session_id`, no `model` key), and no UserPromptSubmit. `/remote-control` has no measured post-condition today and no probe types it (it would open a remote-control link). `/compact` (listed since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows) has the post-condition a SessionStart with source `compact` and the session's own `session_id` (row `local-command-compact`): as measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host in `viola verify`'s Run B (chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row, `evidence/live-round.md`), a pasted `/compact` fires a SessionStart (`source` `compact`, Run B's first `session_id`) and no UserPromptSubmit, its answer read 21 413 ms after the paste; its confirm window is `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL) beside the 10 s `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK`, so a `send` of it is confirmed on a verified CLI and `unconfirmable` at once only on an unverified one. Whether the CLI fires a SessionEnd before that SessionStart is not measured. Skills are not local commands: they expand into a prompt and fire UserPromptSubmit (measured: `/andromeda-arch`).
  - Tag escaping (row `tag-escaping`): the CLI inserts a backslash after `<` in a `pasted_content` tag the user typed, so a literal `<pasted_content` arrives in UserPromptSubmit as `<\pasted_content` and a typed close as `<\/pasted_content`. As measured on 2.1.287, mid-text (chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows, `evidence/step0-shapes.md`), only those two tags were escaped: a typed `<task-notification>` in the middle of a prompt arrived as typed. At the start-of-prompt position, the one the harness classification reads, it arrives as typed too (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host, `evidence/scratch-session.md`), so a human who types it first is filed `harness`. `viola-agent-claude` classifies `harness` on the raw prefix first, then removes any long-paste wrapper with its frame, then un-escapes `<\` before an ASCII letter or `/` when it normalises `prompt-submitted`, so a typed pair is never unwrapped and delivery matching compares plain text. An escaped tag is typed text and never classifies `harness`, with one exception: `<\cross-session-message` is a harness prefix, on the relayed measurement that the cross-session message arrives escaped, `<\cross-session-message from="…" from-name="…">`, as the CLI's own injection — a human who types that tag at a prompt's start is filed `harness` too (founder-ratified, 2026-09-29). On 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host the message arrived unescaped (Harness prompt prefixes above); the escaped form was not seen there and its prefix stays compiled.

  `viola run` learns the CLI version by running the resolved child executable once with `--version` (no user args, stdout and stderr drained through `MAX_FRAME`, killed at 5 s) before spawning it; the first line must read exactly `X.Y.Z (Claude Code)`. Output it cannot parse counts as an unlisted version. The fake agent answers `--version` the same way. A version is verified only when its stamp holds every relied row `pass` (`LedgerRow::relied()`, below); `cli_verified` (and `cli_version` when parsed) is recorded in the snapshot and the `claude-child` `process-start`. On an unverified version viola still types, runs the wheel and emits events, but withholds dialog answers, and drivers get `unverified-cli`. As landed by chunk 2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify and widened by chunks 2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes, 2026-10-05-dialog-rows-and-re-probe, 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows, 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row, 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows and 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, the ledger (`viola_agent_claude::ledger`, a closed set) holds twenty-four rows (the members of `LedgerRow::ALL`, in its order): `shim-resolution` · `spine-hooks` · `session-start-fields` · `prompt-verbatim` · `stop-message` · `largest-hook-payload` · `modal-signature` · `input-box-signature` · `quiet-period` · `confirm-window` · `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency` · `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear` · `paste-newline` · `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `statusline-rate-limits` · `resume-session` · `agents-join` · `local-command-compact`.
 The relied set is `LedgerRow::relied()`, `ALL` filtered in its order by `relied_on(row, statusline::WRAPPED_HERE)`: the three statusline rows are relied only where the status line is wrapped (Unix), so a Unix host relies on all twenty-four rows and a Windows host on twenty-one, the first eighteen, `resume-session`, `agents-join` and `local-command-compact`, the last three relied on every OS.
 `check(row, &Probes)` reads `Probes { print, typed, trusted, dialogs, statusline, resumed, agents }` (`trusted`: Run B's captures in claim order; `statusline`: Run B's status line captures in `k` order; `resumed`: Run E's captures in claim order; `agents`: Run B's one agents capture, an `AgentsCapture`): the `agents-join` row passes only when that capture parses and holds exactly one row whose `pid` is Run B's child pid, whose `sessionId` is the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture and whose status is idle or busy (`agents_joined`), and fails with no capture; the override row passes on at least one capture, the shell row on at least one capture whose every shell verdict is `bin-sh`, and the rate-limits row on a capture whose `rate_limits.five_hour` and `.seven_day` each hold an integer `used_percentage` 0–100 and an integer `resets_at` (`whole_rate_limits`, narrower than `statusline::reading`, which also takes an RFC 3339 string and a fraction), and the resume row only when Run E's first SessionStart capture has `source` `resume` and the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture, taken only when `is_session_id` accepts it (`ledger::resume_target`), and the compact row only when the first SessionStart capture of source `compact` after the newline turn's prompt (`compact_start`) has a non-empty `session_id` equal to that of Run B's first SessionStart capture, no UserPromptSubmit carries `/compact`, and `compact_latency_ms` is within `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (`local_command_compacted`); a run that raised no dialog fails its dialog rows, and a Run B that did not paste a text fails that text's row.
 `viola verify [--record <DIR>] [-- <program> [args…]]` (program default `claude`) first drives ONE print-mode probe, `<program> -p "<PROBE_PROMPT>" --model haiku --plugin-dir <probe>/plugin --no-session-persistence` (cwd the probe dir, 120 s deadline), whose `viola-verify-probe` plugin captures the four spine payloads through the hidden `hook --capture` arm. It then drives five interactive PTY runs (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` and its children under `src/cmd/verify/typed/`). Each is a direct spawn under the R8 strip at a fixed 80×24, its output capped at `MAX_FRAME` into a `Screen` fed under `catch_unwind`. Run A runs untrusted in a fresh 0700 `viola-verify-*` dir under the OS temp dir, with empty input, and is ended by a kill. Once Run B's first turn has settled, before its framing pastes, verify makes ONE `claude agents --json` read (`typed::turns::agents_read`: Run B's program, cwd the probe dir, the R8 strip, `VERSION_DEADLINE`, none once a stop is read), its capture carried in memory and never written to the captures dir, its spawn pair `agents-probe`; no live start is added (a widening of verify's child set the founder ratified himself, his own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, `inputs#I1`, relayed verbatim by the operator); in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it. Run B runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` (0700, a drop guard).
 On a wrapped OS (Unix), and only for shell-plain paths, it also gets one `--settings <probe dir>/typed/statusline.json` after its `--plugin-dir` pair (`typed::runs::trusted_args`; the document `statusline::probe_document` builds, written 0600; Windows passes none), whose `statusLine` command `<pinned viola> hook statusline --capture <probe dir>/typed/statusline --shell "$0"` files each status line payload with its shell verdict through the hidden capture arm ([Hook Contract]); Runs A, C and D keep their arguments and no run is added (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, «Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`). It gets six bracketed pastes, all compiled texts: `PROBE_PROMPT`, then `PROBE_LONG_PASTE` (1 500 bytes, one line), `PROBE_TAG_PASTE` (200 bytes), `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (113 bytes, ASCII, exactly one LF at neither end, no CR), `PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND` (the list's `/compact`) and `PROBE_LOCAL_COMMAND` (the list's `/clear`), each of the five added ones only into rows that hold an input-box literal and no modal literal, none after the stop, each text waited for one more UserPromptSubmit and one more Stop, and each local command for one more SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit, up to `PROBE_DEADLINE` (`ledger::FRAMING_TURNS`, in paste order `paste-1` · `paste-2` · `paste-3` · `compact-1` · `clear-1`); a failed wait ends the added pastes, and verify still makes six starts. The long, tag-like and local-command pastes are the founder's live answer of 2026-10-06T19:38Z, given after the widening was shown, relayed by the overseer. The newline paste is his own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row («Пятая вставка в Run B», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I2`).
 The `/compact` paste is his own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row («Шестая вставка в Run B», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I3`). It is ended by Ctrl-C, Ctrl-C again after 500 ms, then a kill at `PROBE_DEADLINE`; a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`cmd::verify::stop`) is ended by a kill with no key, starts no later run and writes no stamp. Each screen settles at the first `QUIET_PERIOD`-quiet instant holding a compiled literal, else at the first quiet instant past `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, with one exception: after each of Run B's added text turns (the long, the tag-like and the newline turns) and after its `/compact` turn (the rows `/clear` is pasted into) the rows the paste guard reads come from a wait (`Run::box_wait`) that ends only on a `QUIET_PERIOD`-quiet screen holding a compiled literal, on a poisoned screen, or at `PROBE_DEADLINE` from that turn's Stop, so a quiet screen with no literal keeps waiting past `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (the founder's live answer of 2026-10-06T20:49Z, relayed by the overseer). The reason is measured: after a long paste 2.1.287's footer reads `paste again to expand` and holds no input-box literal for 8.0 s from the paste, which was 6.5 s after that turn's Stop (chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows, `evidence/rehearsal-shapes.md`). Verify's `box_wait` is its own wait, bounded by `PROBE_DEADLINE`. The readiness gate of `viola run` ([Screen Model]) waits on the same screen too, up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT` from the send's entry into the gate: since chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint, on a verified CLI a `send` issued while the hint stands (a quiet screen with no compiled literal) is delivered once the input box returns, and a hint that outlasts the bound ends `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed.
 Both are as measured at that chunk: the delivery under the fake agent's 3 000 ms hold (`evidence/hint-red-green.md`), the refusal at the bound on the injected clock in unit cases only. A `send` under the real CLI's hint is as measured on live 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive (`evidence/live-readings.ndjson`, `send-under-hint`): a 32-byte text sent 4 248 ms after a 2 564-byte long paste was issued waited in the gate, was issued 8 319 ms after the paste, and was confirmed (`send-confirmed.duration_ms` 4 081 against the 8 500 ms bound), with no `wheel` record. Before that chunk such a `send` was refused at the first quiet instant, 0.63 s after it was issued on the real CLI (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host, `evidence/hint-window.md`, and under the fake agent at chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-send-outcomes, `evidence/paste-hint-send.md`). The same sequence without the hint was and is delivered. On the real CLI the hint is a timer of 8.0 s from the last long paste (nine timings over the two chunks, 8.000 s to 8.023 s; a second long paste restarts it, a short one does not), 3.8 s to 7.0 s of it after the turn's Stop. A `viola wait` with no cursor issued in the window woke on nothing and ran to its deadline, and `wait --after` the earlier cursor returns the logged turn end at once, inside the window, so the advice of the `input-not-ready` hint line of that time (`viola wait <name>, then send again`) did not lead out of it; the line no longer gives that advice (below). On an unverified CLI the partial gate typed a short text under the hint and the CLI submitted and confirmed it; a long or a repeated text under the hint is unmeasured.
 What `send` does while the hint stands is the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-07T10:29Z (relayed by the overseer), built at chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint: on a verified CLI the gate waits for the input box on a quiet screen with no literal, and the bound is 8.5 s. The fake agent's hold cap rose to 10 000 ms with it. The `input-not-ready` hint line is no longer printed for the paste-hint cause. Its wording for the remaining causes (a modal, a screen that never goes quiet, a poisoned screen, a hint past the bound) is the founder's, landed at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive (`send_hint`, `src/human/hints.rs`): `<name> was not ready for input; send again, and if it repeats a human must look at the session`, in place of the line that advised `viola wait`. Exit code, refusal, detail and `--json` did not change. The moved bound was re-verified by path on 2.1.287 at that chunk (`stamped 2.1.287  17 pass  0 fail`, `evidence/reverify-round.md`). Run C runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-dialogs/` with `--model haiku --settings <DIALOG_SETTINGS>` (an `ask` rule for `Bash(touch viola-probe-permission)`) and the dialog-kind probe plugin, and pastes the three compiled dialog prompts, each after the previous turn's Stop capture; its one `allow` runs that `touch` inside its own dir. Run D runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-plan/` with `--model haiku --permission-mode plan --settings {"plansDirectory":"<Run D dir>/plans"}` (a 0700 `plans/` inside the 0700 dir, so the plan file lands inside the run's own dir and none under `~/.claude/plans`, as measured on 2.1.288 and 2.1.287) and the dialog plugin, and pastes `PLAN_PROMPT`.
 Runs C and D wait for the input box with no modal before any paste; their dialogs are answered only by the probe hook's `--answers` body from the compiled answer table `PROBE_ANSWERS`; after the last Stop is captured the screen settles, as Run B's turn does (a 300 ms quiet grace, not an absolute guarantee), and the run is ended by a kill; each wait is bounded by `PROBE_DEADLINE`. Run E runs last, after Run D (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 2 of chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows, «Run E, шестой старт», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`): it reads Run B's captures and takes the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart through `ledger::resume_target` (only of the session-id shape; with none it spawns nothing and the row fails), and runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/` (0700, a drop guard) with the run args, then `--plugin-dir` and the capture plugin under `<probe dir>/resume/`, then `viola_agent_claude::resume_args(id, false)` (`--resume <id>`), with empty input and no `--settings`; it waits for one SessionStart capture up to `PROBE_DEADLINE`, settles after it and is ended by a kill. As measured on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at that chunk (`evidence/live-round.md`), the CLI found Run B's session from Run E's own `-resume` project directory. No run writes a byte into a CLI dialog, and a start showing a modal is killed with no key (the founder's live rulings of 2026-10-05, relayed by the overseer).
 It checks the relied rows (`check_rows` walks `LedgerRow::relied()`), prints one stdout step line per relied row (`[NN/MM] <row id> <row words>  pass|fail`, `MM` being `LedgerRow::relied().len()`: 24 on Unix, the last `[24/24] local-command-compact …`; 21 on Windows, the last `[21/21] local-command-compact …`) and a `stamped <ver>  N pass  M fail` summary, and writes the stamps through the one writer (the Ledger stamps envelope, Standard Contracts); a failing row still writes its stamp, and verify exits 1. `--record <DIR>` writes the scrubbed `<DIR>/<ver>/<Event>.default.json` fixtures, the dialog captures as `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` variants (`ledger::dialog_variants`), Run B's framing captures as `UserPromptSubmit.paste-<n>.json`, `SessionStart.compact-<n>.json`, `SessionEnd.clear-<n>.json` and `SessionStart.clear-<n>.json` variants (`ledger::framing_variants`), Run B's status line captures as `StatusLine.default-1.json` and `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json` (`ledger::statusline_variants`: the first capture without `rate_limits`, the first that passes the rate-limits row), Run E's first SessionStart as `SessionStart.resume-1.json` (`ledger::resume_variants`), Run B's agents read as `Agents.recorded-1.json` (Run B's own row only, `ledger::agents_variant`) and the signature-only `Screen.<phase>.json` screens the fake agent replays, only when 0 rows fail. subject: dec-cli-version-compatibility
text: - Before its `cli` log opens, `viola verify` runs `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree(home, None, None)` (the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/`, each that exists); a refusal prints the home pair and exits 1 with no step line, no summary and no line. The one stamps writer, `update_stamps`, runs `strict::check_stamps` before it creates `ledger/` and again under its lock before the capped read; a refusal (`StampsError::StrictModes`, [Error Handling]) reads and writes nothing, and verify maps it to the same home pair.

subject: dec-session-liveness
text:
- **[Session Liveness] Heartbeat file primary; pid + process start time decide `gone`, and `claude agents --json` only enriches it.** Rationale: the prototype's heartbeat proved reliable. A bare pid is unsafe because pids get reused, which is why start time is matched too: a snapshot whose pid is dead, or alive with another start time, is `gone` whatever the heartbeat says (Session liveness). `claude agents --json` adds idle/busy status and shows unwrapped sessions as read-only rows. A `viola run` whose `ViolaName` is `live` or `stale` refuses to start (exit 1, with a message naming the instance); once the endpoint exists, a name with an answering endpoint refuses the same way. `viola revive` refuses a `live` or `stale` name through the same collision check and its two stderr pairs, as the first of its four preflight readings (the name's holder, the logged session, `session-live`, the recorded directory; a later reading is not taken once an earlier one refuses). `session-live` (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is one `claude agents --json` read: a row whose `sessionId` is the logged id about to be resumed refuses, `--fork` skips the reading, and a failed read passes (fail open). As measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (that chunk's `evidence/live-p4.md`), a second interactive `claude --resume <id>` of an id a live `claude` holds is neither refused nor copied: both sessions run under the one id, two writers on one transcript, so the reading stays a refusal; and after `/clear` the agents row of the session's pid names the new id (P12 follows), so a session-id join survives a `/clear` because the wrapper rewrites the snapshot's `agent_session_id` on each `session-start`. The strict-modes check on the home and the instance's files runs ahead of them, before the wrapper log opens (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor).
 A revive that passes goes through the same start as `run`, so the collision check runs twice. It resumes the `gone` instance in place: its `events.ndjson` is appended to with the earlier bytes unchanged, no launch is replayed, and its first record is `wheel{holder:"driver", cause:"start"}`, as every start's (the founder's answer, live, 2026-10-10, relayed by the operator: a revived start keeps the wheel at `driver`). Otherwise `run` starts in this order: program resolution (the `.cmd`/`.bat` refusal, which writes nothing), collision check, pinned copy and plugin folder, the ConPTY sideload (Windows x64, fail-open), version gate, exclusive bind of the endpoint (a bind that finds the name taken is an exit-1 refusal, `squatted-name`, so two concurrent starts cannot both win), first snapshot (with `endpoint`, `pinned_bin`, and `statusline_command` when the named source gave a command; `pid`, `started_at`) and heartbeat, the start `wheel` and `budget-gate` events, then the child spawn, after which the snapshot is rewritten with `child_pid`. Between the first snapshot and the spawn `run` also rewrites the per-session settings override (Unix only; §Occupied Resources, Claude Code integration names).
 As landed by 2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify every step has its place (the sideload step added by 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty): program resolution → collision → pinned copy and plugin → ConPTY sideload (`run.conpty_sideload`, Windows: `pin_companions` + the absolute-path pre-load; `outcome` `loaded` · `hash-mismatch` · `strict-modes-failed` · `unreadable` · `load-failed` · `not-built`, never a refusal; its held handles live until `spawn_child` returns) → strip plan → version gate (`run::version_gate`: the bounded `--version` read logged as a `version-probe` `process-start`/`process-exit` pair, the stamps read, `cli_version`/`cli_verified` carried into the first snapshot and the `claude-child` `process-start`; `run` prints nothing on any gate outcome) → endpoint bind → the budget gate at start (span `run.budget_eval` with `trigger: start`; it reads `budget.json`, restores no override and writes nothing; the thresholds were read from `config.json` earlier in the start, each rejection logged then) → first snapshot (its `budget_paused` is that verdict, its `budget_override_until` always absent) → heartbeat → start events (record two, `budget-gate`, carries that verdict's `data`, where it carried the constant `{"paused": false}` before chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor) → spawn, so the child's first SessionStart hook finds a listening endpoint and a recorded snapshot. Since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the start also restores the wrapper's link set before the endpoint serves: it reads `events.ndjson` twice there (`WaitFeed::rebuild`, then `LinkSet::restore`), the first snapshot's `links` is the restored set, the start appends no line for links and its start records are unchanged. `viola revive` starts through the same function, so a revived start's first snapshot carries the logged links.
 A gone instance's directory is reused at once, and its `events.ndjson` is appended to, never truncated.

subject: dec-session-liveness
text: - The snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` are also the server identity: `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` returns them with the endpoint from one `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` (`LiveEndpoint`, only on a real snapshot: a replayed or absent one gives none), and every frame-writing client runs the strict-modes instance check first (the CLI's `client::refuse_untrusted`, [Links]; `viola mcp`'s frame tools, [MCP]; the hook's, [Hook Contract]), then the liveness-only pre-check, then, on Linux and Windows, compares the connected peer's pid and its OS start time with them before its first frame (`verify_server`; §Standard Contracts, Session liveness).

subject: dec-cli-conventions
text: - **[CLI Conventions] Human text by default, `--json` for agents, a typed exit code per refusal. Prompt text comes from stdin or `--file`, never from a leading-slash argument.** viola warns when an argument carries a Git Bash rewritten-path prefix. Rationale: Git Bash rewrites `/skill` arguments into Windows paths (brief §6), and agents need machine-parseable refusals. `viola revive` takes `--json` on both arms (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): a refused strict-modes check or a preflight refusal prints `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing`) in place of its `unable:` / `hint:` pair, exit 1, and `<name> --list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order; without `--json` the pairs and the `--list` rows are byte-identical. A refusal `run`'s start makes after a passed preflight (`batch-script-child`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `squatted-name`, a `claude` not on `PATH` as `internal-error`) prints no document as landed; its document is owed to the working-route entry "Exit-cause code catalogue".

subject: conv-refusal-reason
text:
- **`RefusalReason` (serialised kebab-case):** `human-typing` · `budget-paused` · `unverified-cli` · `not-delivered` · `unknown`. `unknown` is `#[serde(other)]`, so an older client can still read a refusal from a newer wrapper. `detail` values are kebab-case strings from a closed set per reason, extended only in `viola-core`:
  - `human-typing`: `null` · `manual-pause`
  - `budget-paused`: `five-hour` · `seven-day`
  - `unverified-cli`: `null`
  - `not-delivered`: `input-not-ready` · `no-prompt-submitted` · `turn-running` · `unknown-dialog` · `control-character` · `empty-text`
  - `unknown`: a code word (`viola_core::is_code_word`) or `null`

  Readers treat an unrecognised code-word `detail` as opaque text, never as an error. When several refusals apply, the wrapper returns only the first in this order. For `send`: `not-delivered`/`control-character` first (`viola_core::validate_paste_text`: LF, CR and TAB pass; every other C0, DEL and C1 is refused, never stripped; the CLI checks before any frame and the wrapper checks again), then `not-delivered`/`empty-text` (the typed text, the text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters ([Delivery Confirmation]), is empty; the CLI checks before any frame and the wrapper checks again, before the first wheel read; a text that also holds a refused character is still `control-character`), then `human-typing`, `budget-paused`, `not-delivered`/`turn-running` (a turn running, or another `send` in flight), then the readiness gate (`input-not-ready`, also when no child has started), then `human-typing` and `not-delivered`/`turn-running` read a second time once the gate has returned ready, and then the confirmation (`no-prompt-submitted`) outcome. A paste that fails after `send-issued` is `input-not-ready` with that send's `cursor`. For `answer`: `not-delivered`/`control-character` first (`validate_paste_text` on the response's free text; the CLI checks before any frame and the wrapper checks again), then `human-typing`, `unverified-cli`, `not-delivered`/`unknown-dialog`. `unconfirmable` is not a refusal detail. It appears only in an `ok` payload (`{"confirmed":false,"detail":"unconfirmable"}`), for a ledger-listed local command whose post-condition is "none" or not yet measured on this CLI version.

subject: conv-exit-codes
text:
- **CLI exit codes:**
  - `0` ok
  - `1` internal error (anyhow edge), `viola run` refusing to start because its `ViolaName` is `live` or `stale` ([Session Liveness]; `detail:"already-live"`, stderr `unable: <name> is already live` / `hint: viola list`, or `unable: <name> is still running but not answering` with the stale hint), `viola run` refusing a pinned copy that fails its re-hash (`detail:"pinned-hash-mismatch"`, `unable: the pinned viola copy failed its integrity check`), `viola run` refusing a `.cmd`/`.bat` child program before any spawn (`process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"batch-script-child"}`, the two fixed `unable:`/`hint:` stderr lines), and `viola run` losing the exclusive endpoint bind to another holder (`detail:"squatted-name"`, `unable: the endpoint for <name> is held by another process` / `hint: another process holds this name's endpoint; stop it or pick another name`, no path, pid or pipe name); `viola revive` refusing its strict-modes check, which runs before the wrapper log opens and outside the preflight (`unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` and its `hint:` on stderr, exit 1, no log opened and no line written, on the start arm as on `--list`; chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor), and `viola revive` refusing at its preflight, whose four readings (the name's holder, the logged session, `session-live`, the recorded directory;
 chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board added the third) are taken in a fixed order and stop at the first refusal: `detail:"already-live"` (`run`'s own collision check and its two pairs, unchanged), `detail:"no-session"` (two pairs: `unable: <name> has no logged session to resume`, and `unable: <name> has no logged session with that id` for an `--id` the log does not hold), `detail:"session-live"` (`unable: <name>'s session is open in another claude` / `hint: close it there first, or start a copy: viola revive <name> --fork`, the founder's wording, his own answer to P4 fork 4 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, `inputs#I1`; one `claude agents --json` read lists the logged id live in another `claude`; skipped under `--fork`; a failed read passes) and `detail:"cwd-missing"` (`unable: <name>'s recorded directory is missing`), each one `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr that holds no recorded directory, pid or logged id and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail}` in `run-<name>.ndjson`; under `--json` each of these revive refusals, the strict-modes one included, is instead one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing`; `client::refused_document`) with stderr empty, the same exit 1 and the same log lines, while a refusal `run`'s start makes after a passed preflight prints no document (owed to "Exit-cause code catalogue"; chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract) (`viola revive --list` has two refusals: the strict-modes check, the stderr pair or its document and exit 1 with no log line, and `no-session`, the stderr pair or its document and exit 1 with, under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`, `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"no-session"}` in the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson`);
 `viola verify` with a failing ledger row (its stamp still written, last stdout line `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail`), `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM before its rows are checked (no stamp written, stdout empty, stderr exactly `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI`, and `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` when `VIOLA_NAME` holds a valid name; chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup) and verify's refusals, each an `unable:` + `hint:` pair on stderr with no path: `the claude CLI was not found` / `install Claude Code or put it on PATH`, `the claude CLI is a .cmd or .bat script` / `pass the real executable, not a .cmd or .bat shim`, `the CLI version could not be read` / `run claude --version to check the install`, `a recorded fixture is not clean: <file> <code>` (a screen: `<file> row <n>[ seam] <code>`; codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`; never the content) / `record with a viola home under your user home`, plus run's pinned-copy re-hash refusal; and the `cli` role's internal error: `src/main.rs` `role_of` files every first word but `run`, `revive`, `mcp`, `hook` and a leading `-` flag under `cli` (a first word `mcp`, after any `--home <dir>` / `--home=<dir>`, is `Role::Mcp`, whose exit maps like `Other` and which never prints `error: internal error` — `prints_internal_error` stays `Cli`-only; chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers), and `revive` followed (after any `--home` pair) by `--list` before a `--` under `cli` too (every other `revive` is a wrapper beside `run`, and its start arm logs as process `run`; a `--list` after `--` is the child's word;
 so `send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`, `verify`, `revive --list` and `plugin install`), and a dispatch `Err` or a caught panic in any of them prints exactly `error: internal error` on stderr once, from the `main` catch site, no hint — no dispatch arm prints it; for `viola wait` / `viola last` exit 1 also covers a refusal reply, a reply of no known shape, and any channel error but a failed connect or a closed / reset connection (those are exit 21); for `viola link` / `viola unlink` exit 1 also covers a refusal reply and an `ok` of another shape than the verb's (`link`: a string `since` and a boolean `already_linked`; `unlink`: an object); for `viola list` exit 1 covers an `instances/` that exists and cannot be listed (or an entry whose type cannot be read) and a log start that fails, while a per-instance read error gives no row (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list)
  - `2` usage error (clap, a second positional to `viola send` included; never produced by `viola hook`), and `viola send` text over `MAX_FRAME` or not UTF-8 (`error: the text must be readable UTF-8 of at most 16 MiB`)
  - `10` `human-typing`
  - `11` `budget-paused`
  - `12` `unverified-cli`
  - `13` `not-delivered`
  - `14` `unknown` refusal
  - `20` protocol fault from the wrapper, a `-32602` from `link` / `unlink` included (a missing, non-string or invalid name, a `driven` that is not the serving wrapper's own name, or a `driver` equal to `driven`: the self-pair is refused by the wrapper only, never client-side)
  - `21` instance unreachable (no live endpoint for the `ViolaName`); also `viola list`'s refused strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance, which refuses the whole board (`--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`, no log opened) — the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list's planning, superseded 2026-10-13); `viola plugin install`'s refused strict-modes check of the home or an existing `marketplace/` tree dir is the same exit and document (human mode the home-state pair; nothing created, no log opened); `viola link` / `viola unlink`'s refused instance check of the driven instance (`check_instance` on the home and `instances/<driven>`, before any role file or log opens) is the same exit and document (human mode the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair; no log opened, no line written, the mode left as found): exit 21 as for `list` and `plugin install`, not `revive`'s exit 1

subject: conv-exit-codes
text: - Exit `21` also covers, on `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink`, a server that is not the recorded wrapper (the connected peer's pid or OS start time is not the snapshot's, or the check cannot be made): no frame is written, and the verb prints the same `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` under `--json` with stderr empty, or the `unable  <name>  instance-unreachable` line with the server-verify hint last on stderr (its wording: design-system, surface cli-send). The client's own refusals (exit 13) and the strict-modes instance check (exit 21, `client::refuse_untrusted`: the target instance for `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release`, the driven instance for `link` / `unlink`) come first, before any connect, and the cause has no exit code, `--json` code or `RefusalReason` of its own.

subject: conv-exit-codes
text: - Exit `21` also covers the refused strict-modes check of `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` (`client::refuse_untrusted`: `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`, the verb's first step, after its text read for `send`): human mode prints `link`'s instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair, and `--json` exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` with stderr empty; nothing under the home is opened and no line is written.

subject: conv-mcp-results
text:
- **MCP:** a success is a tool result with `isError: false` and the channel `ok` payload as `structuredContent` (for `list`, the caller-side `{items, budget, skipped}` payload, the `list` payload of Standard Contracts). A refusal is a tool result with `isError: true` and the same `refusal` + `detail` in `structuredContent`. An unreachable instance and a wrapper protocol fault are also `isError: true` tool results. Their `structuredContent` is `{"error":"instance-unreachable"|"wrapper-fault","detail":…}`, the same as CLI `--json` (`instance-unreachable` with `detail: null`; `wrapper-fault` with the JSON-RPC fault's `{code,message,data}` as `viola_channel::sanitised_fault` reads it: a fixed `message`, `data` a closed object or null). As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): each handler re-validates its raw argument object (`target` through `ViolaName::try_new`, `text` a string, `after` / `timeout_ms` absent, `null` or a `u64`, `dialog_id` a `u64`, `response` an object through `Response::parse`), and a failure is an `isError: true` result `{"error":"invalid-params","detail":"<field>"}` (the closed field words `target` · `text` · `after` · `timeout_ms` · `dialog_id` · `response`) with no frame written; every `isError` text is `refused: <code>`. JSON-RPC errors are the MCP connection's own faults, an unknown tool name (`-32602`) and an internal handler fault — any other channel error, a reply of no known shape, a `wait` / `last` refusal, a panicked call — which is `-32603` `internal error` with `data: null`. `tools/list`'s result carries `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private`: claude 2.1.287 negotiates protocol `2026-07-28` and drops every tool of a list result without them (as measured live at that chunk, `evidence/live-mcp.md` start 1).
 claude 2.1.302 on that protocol opens with `server/discover` (its JSON-RPC id a string) and then `tools/list`, each carrying `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`, `…/clientInfo`, `…/clientCapabilities`), and sends no `initialize` or `notifications/initialized`; viola's two results each carry `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private` (as measured live at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii/evidence/live-tap.md`, start 2). That recorded exchange, `fixtures/claude/2.1.302/Mcp.tools-list-1.json`, is replayed against `viola mcp` by `tests/mcp_recorded_exchange.rs` (`viola-e2e`), which takes the `tools/list` response by its request's id and holds the served result to the recorded result's key and type shape, its tool names in order.
